newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai mayor sees unemployment rising by 25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai mayor sees unemployment rising by 25 pct.

text.p: The ranks of Shanghai's jobless will swell by 25 percent this year and the city's services sector will be unable to generate enough jobs for the surplus manpower, Shanghai Mayor Xu Kuangdi said on Monday.

Unemployment will reach 250,000 by the end of 1996, up from 200,000 at the end of 1995, Xu said at the end of a meeting of the International Business Leaders' Advisory Council, which meets once a year to advise the Shanghai city government.
Shanghai's resident population at the end of 1995 was 14.15 million, official figures show.
Xu said that from 1992 to the end of 1995, 870,000 people lost their jobs in traditional state factories but 670,000 of them were re-trained and found work elsewhere.
The Liberation Daily newspaper, in a commentary published on Monday, said redundant workers are needed in the city's service sector, which is booming.
It said jobs are proliferating in domestic services, food preparation and delivery, dry cleaning, electrical appliance repair and clothes mending, it said.

However, in a speech during the meeting, Xu said the services sector would likely be unable to generate enough jobs for all of those put out of work in state-owned textile and other light industrial factories.
"Even though great efforts have been made to re-employ more laid-off workers, Shanghai is still facing great pressure," Xinhua news agency quoted him as saying.
Xu said one reason for Shanghai's unemployment problem is that the city's industries have seen their share of national markets shrink as other areas of China industrialise.
From the 1950s to the 1970s, goods made in Shanghai held a 25 percent share of China's total domestic market but that figure has fallen to only six percent, Xu said.
